title: Common Probability Distributions
interviewAnswer: Know when Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Normal and related distributions are appropriate. The distribution is a model for the data-generating process, not merely a curve-fitting choice.
why: Interviewers use distributions to test whether you can connect a mathematical model to how data is generated instead of selecting a curve by habit.
intuition: A distribution describes the values a random variable can take and how probability is allocated across them. Choose the family from the mechanism: binary event → Bernoulli, number of successes in fixed trials → Binomial, event counts in an interval → Poisson, continuous additive noise → often approximately Normal.
deepDive: Bernoulli models one binary trial; Binomial sums independent Bernoulli trials with constant success probability; Poisson models counts under a constant event-rate approximation; Normal is continuous and symmetric and often appears through aggregation; Exponential models waiting time between Poisson-process events. Real data may violate independence, constant rate, or symmetry assumptions, so goodness-of-fit and domain reasoning matter.
math:
Bernoulli: P(X=x)=p^x(1-p)^(1-x)
Binomial: P(X=k)=C(n,k)p^k(1-p)^(n-k)
Poisson: P(X=k)=e^{-λ} λ^k/k!
Normal: X ~ N(μ,σ²)
workedExample: Number of support tickets per hour might be modeled as Poisson only if arrivals are roughly independent with a stable rate. If ticket volume has strong time-of-day effects or bursts, a single Poisson model is a poor description.
code:
import numpy as np
rng=np.random.default_rng(0)
print(rng.binomial(n=20,p=.1,size=5))
print(rng.poisson(lam=3,size=5))
commonMistakes: Assuming every continuous variable should be Normal.
Using a distribution without checking its support or assumptions.
Confusing probability density with probability for continuous variables.
followUps: When is Poisson a reasonable model?
What is the relationship between Bernoulli and Binomial?
Why does the Normal distribution appear so often?
What distribution would you use for waiting times?
production: Distribution assumptions influence uncertainty estimates, anomaly thresholds, simulation, forecasting, and likelihood-based losses. Monitor whether the production distribution still resembles the one used during modeling.
